answer: The `SB_DISABLE_SERVICE_WORKER` switch enables online-only mode. The memory says it means no service worker, so there is no offline support and a network round-trip on every operation. It doesn't spell out the effect on sync beyond that.
block:
--- ADR/001 Offline-First PWA.md ---
Context | Context
SilverBullet aims to be **offline-first**: it should keep working with no network and feel instant. While we may reach a point in the state of the world some day where Internet connectivity is always available, we’re not there yet. You should be able to access your notes even when you’re in the middle of a dessert, top of a mountain, or 10km deep in the sea. For that, the client keeps a full local copy of your [[Space]] files and keeps working when the server is unreachable. (This offline-first stance later drove the v2 decision to run *all* application logic in the client — see [[ADR/007 Core Application Logic on the Client]].)

--- ADR/001 Offline-First PWA.md ---
Context | Alternatives considered
* **Online-only (no service worker).** Rejected: no offline support and a network round-trip on every operation — defeats the offline-first goal. (Still available deliberately via `SB_DISABLE_SERVICE_WORKER`.)
* **Bundle a native runtime for offline.** Rejected: heavier and platform-specific. A PWA delivers offline on every platform from one codebase.

--- PWA.md ---
What the PWA gives you | How offline works
SilverBullet’s [[Sync]] engine keeps configured space content in the browser’s IndexedDB. Pages are synchronized by default. Documents and ignored paths have different rules. When online, changes are continuously synced between the browser and the server. When offline, you work against the local copy. On reconnection, the sync engine reconciles any changes.

A service worker caches the application code itself, so even the SilverBullet UI loads without a network connection.

See also: [[Sync]], [[Collaboration]] (what happens to your offline edits when you reconnect), [[Architecture]]

--- PWA.md ---
What the PWA gives you | Limits
Offline startup requires a secure context (HTTPS or localhost), a working service worker and previously cached application code. Plain LAN HTTP runs online-only. See [[TLS#LAN HTTP (no TLS)]]. Installing the PWA does not change these requirements.

Server-backed [[Search]], shell execution, remote sharing and external network APIs require a connection. Local page navigation, editing and queries over the client Object Index can work with cached data. Let the initial sync finish and test the pages and attachments you need before relying on offline access. Browser storage is not a backup.

--- ADR/007 Core Application Logic on the Client.md ---
Context | Alternatives considered
* **Keep the dual-mode (server + sync) architecture.** Rejected: maintaining two PlugOS runtimes in parity was the core pain — an ongoing maintenance burden and a source of subtle bugs. It was also confusing for plug developers.
* **Make *server mode* the only mode** (thin client, the server does everything). Rejected: defeats offline-first and the run-anywhere goal, and keeps the product tied to an always-available, more capable backend.
